claims: NASA is targeting April 1, 2026, for the launch of the crewed Artemis II mission, according to NASA (.gov) and SpaceNews.
Daily launch windows for the Artemis II mission are available through April 6, 2026, according to NASA (.gov) and SpaceNews.
The SLS rocket has returned to Pad 39B for final preparations for the 10-day Artemis II mission around the Moon, according to Florida Today and Spaceflight Now.
NASA (.gov) says the target launch date for Artemis II is April 1, 2026 (No Earlier Than).
NASA (.gov) says launch opportunities for Artemis II extend through April 6, 2026.
SpaceNews notes the next opportunity for Artemis II is April 30, 2026.
NASA (.gov) says the launch site for Artemis II is Kennedy Space Center, Florida (Pad 39B).
NASA (.gov) reports the Artemis II mission goal is a 10-day flight crewed by four astronauts to test Orion spacecraft systems around the Moon.
The Artemis II crew is Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen, according to the Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex.
The rocket and Orion capsule were transported back to the launch pad around March 20, 2026, following final checkouts, according to NASA (.gov) and Florida Today.
